title: Puzzles
why_it_matters: Puzzles test logical thinking and constraint satisfaction. They appear in TCS NQT and Infosys reasoning sections.

misconceptions.signature: Student assumes minimum values without proving feasibility.
Student ignores one constraint while solving.

captain_byte.intro: Puzzles are constrained logic. List constraints, then test candidates.
wrong: Eliminate candidates that violate any constraint.
captain_byte.after_break: You found the missed constraint. Now rebuild the candidate set.
captain_byte.after_mastery: You can now solve logical puzzles. That's placement-ready reasoning skill.
captain_byte.retry_prompt: Try again. Write down all constraints before testing candidates.

steps.narration: Four people sit in a row. A sits left of B. C is between A and D. D is at the right end.

interaction.explanation: This is a sample puzzle. Fix D at right. C between A and D. A left of B.

discover.conclusion: List all constraints. Fix any absolute positions. Test candidates against every constraint. Eliminate violators.

understand: Puzzles use absolute and relative constraints. Common patterns: seating, ranking, assignment, and scheduling. Use tables or diagrams to track possibilities.

manipulate.prompt: A is taller than B. C is shorter than A. B is taller than D. Who is the tallest?
manipulate.hint: A > B, A > C, B > D. So A is tallest.

predict.prompt: Five people sit in a line. P is left of Q. R is between P and S. T is at the right end. Who is second from right?

build.prompt: Four people have different heights. A is taller than B. C is shorter than D. B is taller than C. D is not the tallest. Rank them.
build.explanation: From constraints: A > B, A > C, B > C, D > C, D not tallest → A tallest, D second, B third, C fourth.

break_step.prompt: A student says B is tallest because B > D. What is wrong?
break_step.correct_reasoning: A > B, so B cannot be tallest.

debug.correct_reasoning: A is tallest because A > B and A > C.

retrieval.prompt: What is the first step in solving a puzzle?

transfer.prompt: Three people have different amounts of money. A has more than B. C has less than A. B has more than C. Who has the least?
transfer.explanation: A > B > C or A > C and B > C. Either way, C is lowest.

practice.prompt: A is taller than B. C is shorter than B. Who is tallest?
P is left of Q. R is right of Q. Who is in the middle?
Practice 1: Apply Puzzles to solve this problem.
practice.explanation: This demonstrates Puzzles in a placement context.

proof.prompt: Four people A, B, C, D have different ranks. A is higher than B. C is lower than A. D is higher than C but lower than B. Find the ranking.
Prove your Puzzles skill: explain the solution to this problem.

proof_questions.prompt: TCS: Five people sit around a table. A is right of B. C is opposite D. E is left of A. Find E's position.
proof_questions.explanation: Use fixed references and relative positions.
